chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:
The woman whose husband has died, she observes the waiting period when the news reaches her, because she intends to mourn for him.
ai.seo_question: When does a widow's waiting period begin according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the iddah for a widow whose husband died while absent begins upon the receipt of news, emphasizing that the core objective is mourning (i'tidad). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential focus on the widow's actual knowledge and intent rather than a fixed calendar count from the moment of death, distinguishing it from cases where the husband is present. It underscores the practical application of iddah as a period of emotional transition and preparation for remarriage.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Nasr, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The woman widowed from her husband should observe the waiting period when it (news) reaches her because she would want to mourn over him’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu Nasr who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan, al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
A woman whose husband dies must begin counting her waiting period from the day the news reaches her as well as mourning for him.’”
